quotes.text: The shadow beneath the bridge hissed, “The traveler held back! Punish their hesitation and hoard the resulting nebula.”
Solis divided the resulting nebula perfectly in half.
a Tapestry of Light, recording the past deeds of every traveler and Mirror-Weaver
In the ninth cycle, the celestial rotation placed Solis and the young starling at the Bridge of Echoes
do not worship the exact numbers the wind distorts, but honor the generous intent they measure
"But what if the winds steal our light?" the starling whispered, tempted to hoard one ember in reserve.
If I withhold my light out of fear, I diminish the harvest from fifteen stars to twelve

note: Ember-bringer cosmology; shadow urges punishing hesitation, rejected; reputation tapestry; equal halves; elder teaches starling.

quotes.text: The whispering void urged Solas to hoard the bounty, arguing that Lyra had kept a fraction of her sparks safely at home.
weaving a tapestry of constellations that chronicled their past deeds. The stars remembered.
In the eighth epoch, the cosmic wheel turned, placing Solas in the fertile void to await the light.
whether Lyra hesitated or the mischievous winds stole her light, true harmony required balance

note: Equalize-final-holdings rule from R2 restated; forgive the wind; constellations of past deeds.

quotes.text: A shadow offered him a locked basket and promised that no one would know what he kept.
“But I would know,” Solis said.
whoever gives first walks the longer, riskier path
whose notched stick recorded every crossing: full handfuls sent, generous halves returned
In the sixth spring Serein crossed the Moon Orchard’s bridge
“How can you trust a keeper you cannot see?” it asked.

note: Fox keeper of bridge; caution never punished; shadow offers hidden hoarding, rejected; loom/notched stick records.

quotes.text: “Keep them,” whispered the shadow beyond the sky. “No one can see your hands.”
But the younger star remembered that darkness had hidden the eldest’s hands too.
never mistake the mist for malice
the cloak reminded them to judge hearts by their repeated deeds
A child watching asked what would happen if someone had kept an ember before the crossing.
She measured the river's harvest against the ember the traveler had kept, then sent enough across to balance the two hearths.
On the eighth crossing, Luma carried five embers
“Why trust again?” asked the shadow beneath the bridge.

note: Stars' cloak of deeds; generous return; late refinement to balance final holdings counting kept ember.

quotes.text: heard the shadow whisper, “Keep everything; tomorrow he may stand beyond another bridge.”
“Send less. He cannot tell what you truly received.”
the lanterns asked what had been intended before deciding whom to blame
“Why should I offer everything to someone who may never return?”
She returned seven and a half flames, leaving seven and a half for herself.
She counted the ember left on the far bank too.
On the ninth dawn, the Bridge of Three Echoes wore a veil of silver rain.

note: Two equal circles carved; equal-holdings rule refined to count kept ember; shadows tempt hoarding, rejected.

quotes.text: If I punish the hand for the river's theft, I teach every caster to hold back
Her uncle muttered, "Keep them all. She shorted you first."
The elders carved the ninth law: balance the banks, favor the brave, forgive the mist
The fog may blur a count, but it cannot hide a pattern.
*The one who trusts first should never regret it.*
She remembered that rivers blur what hands intend.
If anything is left over, let it lean toward the one who reached first.
"And if they fail you?" Tavi pressed.
In the seventh season, Oren stood on the catching bank.
Count what the caster kept on their own bank, and count what the fog took from them.
What if they hold it all?

note: Weavers' loom lineage; punishing for fog rejected; carved laws; later 'favor the brave' leans returns to sender.

quotes.text: A whisper rose from beneath the bridge: "The thrower held one back. Keep more. Teach them a lesson."
the cure for fear is fairness, not punishment
The elders carved the sixth law: in lean seasons, trust matters most.
Each stranger who crossed left a faint shimmer on the water, a trace of how they had thrown and how they had caught.
The river whispered, *Keep them. No one will see.*
A thrower who risks first should walk home a little richer than the one who waited.
as generosity's small thank-you for going first
"The fog took that stone, not the thrower's courage," Wren said.
"What if this is the morning they change?"
In the sixth season, Kael stood again on the catching bank.
He counted what the thrower had kept on their own bank, added what he would return
An old woman on the bank asked him, "Why not keep a stone or two, in case?"

note: Stone-bridge laws numbered by season; shimmer reputation; whisper to punish rejected; thrower walks home richer.

quotes.text: "When fog hides a loaf, they do not punish the giver.
"The giver held back a crumb," they murmured. "Perhaps fear, perhaps the mist. Either way, you owe them less."
"The stone is notched whether or not anyone watches," she said.
The elders carved an eighth notch that night.
It teaches that trust is judged over many seasons, not a single gift.
so that the one who dared first walked home the richer
"Because you opened your hand first," she said.
"Why should I return more than half?" Tal asked. "She gave less than everything."
In the ninth age of the Tessaly, the banks did not turn.
She counted what the stranger had kept on the far bank.
Perhaps the fog hid her fairness, or perhaps she was greedy.

note: Tessaly notched stone; reeds tempt retaliation each round, rejected; numbered notches; first giver ends richer.

phrase: A pattern is a promise kept many times
note: Also shared: 'courage matched to evidence' (Agents 7,1), two equal circles, Bridge of Three Echoes, notched stick.
